title: Tonno alla Siciliana
subtitle: Sicilian tuna steaks with tomato, olives, capers, and herbs
excerpt: Tonno alla siciliana is a quick Sicilian braise of fresh tuna steaks in a sauce of tomato, olives, capers, and oregano. The tuna goes in last and cooks gently in the sauce for 8 to 10 minutes. It should be just cooked through and still moist in the centre.
sourceNotes: Tuna has been fished in Sicilian waters for centuries, most notably in the annual mattanza (tuna hunt) practised in western Sicily, particularly around Trapani and the Egadi Islands. Sicilian tuna preparations are among the most documented Italian fish dishes, and the combination of tuna with olives, capers, and tomato is a classic agrodolce-adjacent flavour combination of the island. The dish appears in Anna Tasca Lanza's The Heart of Sicily (1993) and other Sicilian culinary references.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the sauce ahead. Add the tuna and cook just before serving.

content.text: Tonno alla siciliana is a Sicilian braise of fresh tuna steaks in a gutsy sauce of tomato, olives, capers, and dried oregano. The sauce is built first and simmered until thick, then the tuna steaks are laid in and cooked gently for 8 to 10 minutes. The tuna should be just cooked through, not overdone and dry. Serve with bread or roasted potatoes.

items.prepNote: about 150 g each, 2 to 2.5 cm thick

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes until pale gold.
Add the tinned tomatoes, crushing them into the pan. Add the olives, capers, and oregano. Season with salt. Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened.

Season the tuna steaks lightly with salt. Lay them in the sauce. Cover and cook over low to medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, spooning sauce over the top halfway through, until the tuna is just cooked through. It should be pale pink in the very centre at most.
Scatter parsley over the top. Serve from the pan with bread or potatoes.

Sicily is one of the main tuna-fishing centres of the Mediterranean. Tuna dishes appear in Sicilian cooking more than in any other Italian region. The combination with olives, capers, and tomato is a Sicilian signature. The annual tuna hunt, known as the mattanza, has been practised off the western coast for centuries. Declining stocks have made it rare today.
